text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Ruling party Kenya African National Union (KANU) dominates parliamentary and civic by-elections retaining the Kitutu Chache constituency in western Kisii district and taking 23 out of 43 civic seats countrywide.
- A couple are killed in their sleep when a lorry veers off the main road and ploughs into their home near Nairobi.
- Armed gangsters kill five people and injure 10 others in raids at two trading centres in Machakos town, eastern Kenya.
- Two policemen shoot dead an Irish Catholic monk they had gone to rescue from a gang of 15 armed thugs.
- President Daniel arap Moi tells the Nairobi City Council to allow the privatisation of garbage collection in the country with immediate effect.

- An opposition MP Njehu Gatabaki of FORD-Asili says it is unfair that Lonrho Holdings sell its 50.2 percent stake in Express Kenya to a joint venture company owned by Swiss and South African firms instead of selling it to Kenyan investors.
- Mary Odinga is appointed permanent representative to Habitat. She replaces Pamela Mboya who retired from the post last year.
- Jackson Mulinge, outgoing Lands and Settlement minister, says a land amendment bill aimed at curbing the rampant irregular plots allocations in the country is set to be tabled in Parliament.
